name: Food Price Pressure (exploratory)
note: Food Price Pressure (exploratory) measures provincial food price pressure, not food insecurity. HIGH means the province's food inflation (PSA, year on year) was above 4 percent, the ceiling of the BSP inflation target, which is a headline-inflation target and not a food-specific one. The 4 percent rule is a tool-adopted default; it is not adviser-endorsed and not validated. High food inflation does not prove hunger, and low food inflation does not prove adequate food.
status: EXPERIMENTAL; tool-adopted default rule (food CPI YoY > 4%, BSP target ceiling); not adviser-endorsed; not validated; measures food price pressure, not food insecurity

D5_sensitivity_information_only.rule: reported only; the 4% threshold is not changed

limitations: Food price pressure is not food insecurity: high food inflation does not prove hunger and low food inflation does not prove adequate food.
The 4% rule is the BSP headline-inflation target ceiling applied to provincial food inflation; it is a tool-adopted default, not adviser-endorsed and not validated.
Skill is not demonstrated for any target at either lead; persistence is the stronger forecast for food inflation and regional hunger.
Probabilities are shrunk toward the climatological rate (fewer than 8 prior forecast dates exist for Platt calibration), and no 80% interval could be issued (fewer than 8 prior residual dates).
About 5-9 independent dates per target and lead; the five provinces share the regional hunger value.
